stories.headline: S&P 500 SLIPS -0.14% TO 7,599 AS ADP +122K AND STRONG ISM LOCK OUT NEAR-TERM FED CUTS
stories.body: ADP private payrolls added 122,000 jobs in May — above the 120,000 consensus — while ISM services data came in stronger than expected, collectively repricing Fed cut odds further out and lifting the DXY to 99.40, a two-month high. The S&P 500 gave back -0.14% from near-record territory as gold fell -1.1% to $4,440 on rising real yields; Friday's nonfarm payrolls now carry outsized importance, with even an in-line print likely to confirm no June or July Fed action.

stories.headline: WTI SURGES TO $96 ON THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION OF IRAN-DRIVEN HORMUZ RISK PREMIUM
stories.body: WTI crude climbed above $95 for a third consecutive session as U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks remain suspended and the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption — characterized by the IEA as the largest in market history — continues to support a premium in prompt-month contracts. The OECD released its 2026 Economic Outlook this morning, cutting global growth to 2.8% from 3.4% and warning that persistent Hormuz disruptions could compress growth to 2.1%; Brent crossed $98, and WTI at $96 materially reprices H2 PCE inflation expectations and further delays Fed easing.

stories.headline: BROADCOM AI REVENUE HITS $10.7B (+140% YOY); Q3 GUIDE $29.4B BLOWS PAST $24B CONSENSUS
stories.body: Broadcom reported record Q2 FY2026 results after the bell, with AI semiconductor revenue growing 140% year-over-year to approximately $10.7 billion, driven by custom accelerators for hyperscaler infrastructure buildouts. The company guided Q3 revenue to $29.4 billion — well above the $24 billion consensus — providing the clearest signal yet that AI capital expenditure is accelerating despite broader macro headwinds. AVGO's results are the most consequential AI earnings read-through of the quarter after the Magnificent Seven cycle.

stories.headline: TRUMP 10% TARIFF WALL ON 60 ECONOMIES ADDS THIRD HEADWIND; SPACEX EYES $1.75T IPO NEXT WEEK
stories.body: The Trump administration's proposed 10% tariff floor on imports from 60 economies adds an inflationary layer on top of the Hormuz oil shock and sticky services inflation, with markets now pricing three simultaneous macro headwinds from near-record equity levels. Separately, SpaceX is targeting a $1.75 trillion IPO valuation as early as next week, a capital event drawing liquidity away from risk assets at a fragile moment for market breadth, even as Broadcom's blowout after-hours print signals AI infrastructure spending remains immune to the macro gravity.

stories.headline: SUMMER PORTAL HEATS UP: KENTUCKY, DUKE LEAD EARLY STANDINGS; UW HAS THREE SPOTS LEFT
stories.body: College basketball enters its summer recruiting window with Kentucky — boosted by Momcilovic's portal commitment — and Duke leading Andy Katz's early 2026-27 Power 44 rankings. Washington, coming off a 16-17 season, has added Watts (Texas Tech), Venters (Gonzaga), Friedrichsen, and Beasley via the portal but has three roster spots remaining before fall practice; the Huskies were not among finalists for No. 1 recruit Tyran Stokes, who is choosing between Oregon, Kentucky, and Kansas.

stories.headline: NBA FINALS GAME 1 TIPS OFF TONIGHT: KNICKS VS. SPURS, 8:30 PM ET — NEW YORK'S FIRST FINALS IN 27 YEARS
stories.body: The 2026 NBA Finals tip off tonight at 8:30 PM ET on ABC in San Antonio, matching Jalen Brunson's Knicks — in their first Finals appearance since 1999 after 11 straight playoff wins — against Victor Wembanyama and the 62-win Spurs, who won unanimous DPOY and finished 3rd in MVP voting. San Antonio eliminated the defending champion Thunder in seven games; New York swept Cleveland in the East Finals. Game 2 is Thursday night. The matchup is the most anticipated Finals opener in nearly a decade.

stories.headline: SEAHAWKS SIGN ENTIRE DRAFT CLASS INCLUDING FIRST-ROUND WR JADARIAN PRICE; MINICAMPS OPEN LEAGUE-WIDE
stories.body: Super Bowl LX champion Seattle has signed their entire 2026 draft class, including first-round WR Jadarian Price, as mandatory minicamps begin league-wide. The Seahawks' final OTA day is tomorrow before their June 9-11 mandatory minicamp. In Pittsburgh, guard Jamaree Salyer was carted off practice with an undisclosed injury, raising O-line depth concerns; 19 more teams begin three-day minicamps next week ahead of training camps.

stories.headline: HUSKIES LAND 4-STAR WR TRE MOORE (2027); PORTAL CYCLE CLOSES WITH 3,664 ENTRANTS NATIONWIDE
stories.body: Washington secured a commitment from 4-star WR Tre Moore of Pflugerville Weiss (TX) — rated No. 23 WR nationally in the 2027 class by 247Sports at 6'3"/200 lbs — the Huskies' highest-rated offensive commit in the class. Nationally, the 2026 transfer portal cycle is effectively closed with 3,664 entrants and 76% committed; LSU topped early program rankings under Lane Kiffin after landing QB Sam Leavitt and 24 portal additions, while Deion Sanders added ex-Texas WR DeAndre Moore to Colorado's revamped roster.

deepDive.title: The Hormuz Risk Premium: How Oil Markets Price Geopolitical Supply Disruptions
content: WTI crude hit $96 per barrel today — up more than $5 in three sessions — as U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks remain suspended and the Strait of Hormuz supply disruption shows no near-term resolution. For a session where gold fell and the dollar strengthened (signs of deflationary tightening), the persistence of high crude seems counterintuitive. But crude and gold respond to different drivers: real yields suppress gold, but oil has its own distinct pricing mechanism — the geopolitical risk premium — that can override broader macro gravity and inject inflationary pressure at the worst possible time for a Fed already on hold.

A geopolitical risk premium is the extra price embedded in crude contracts above the supply-demand equilibrium to compensate for the probability of a supply shock. The Strait of Hormuz processes roughly 21 million barrels per day — about 20% of global oil consumption and over a third of all seaborne LNG. When the strait faces physical or diplomatic constraint, prompt-month futures trade at a premium to longer-dated contracts in a structure called backwardation, because traders bid up near-term delivery to hedge against disruption. WTI's current front-month contract trading $3–4 above the 12-month strip is a real-time proxy for how much insurance the market is buying — and that premium has been widening, not narrowing, across three consecutive sessions.

The clearest historical analogue is the 2019 Abqaiq attack, when drone strikes took out roughly 5% of global supply in a single event, sending crude up 15% overnight before recovery within weeks as Saudi Aramco restored capacity. The key structural difference today: a Hormuz disruption is not episodic — it affects all Gulf producers simultaneously (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iraq, Kuwait, and Iran), making geographic diversification impossible. The IEA's characterization of this as 'the largest supply disruption in market history' reflects that irreplaceability. The 2022 Russian gas cutoff to Europe was comparable in shock magnitude but geographically isolated; the Strait of Hormuz has no bypass.

For the current macro setup, $96 WTI is maximally inconvenient. A sustained price above $90 adds roughly 40–50 basis points to headline CPI year-over-year in the months following — injecting inflationary pressure into an economy where ADP just printed +122K, ISM services beat consensus, and the Fed is already holding rates elevated. The transmission mechanism runs: Hormuz risk premium → elevated crude → elevated gasoline → headline CPI → delayed Fed easing → stronger dollar → compressed growth (the OECD's 2.8% base case drops to 2.1% in the Hormuz stress scenario). That feedback loop, running quietly in the background behind tonight's NBA Finals tip-off, is the clearest real-world example of how a chokepoint 8,000 miles away rewrites domestic monetary policy.
